notes: PSA 6.7 ng/mL. PI-RADS 4. PSAD 0.20. Prostate volume 36 mL. csPCa 0.79.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prior prostate cancer diagnosis with recent PSA rise to 6.7 ng/mL and new MRI findings.

The patient is a 68-year-old retired butcher, widowed but living with a partner, who presents for re-evaluation of his prostate cancer. He has a history of type 2 diabetes managed with empagliflozin, chronic kidney disease with an eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2, and benign prostatic hyperplasia with an IPSS score of 16/35. He is a non-smoker, consumes 2 units of alcohol per week, and maintains an active lifestyle by running 3x/week. He has had stable cardiology reviews in autumn 2024 and recently completed an audiology hearing test. His next-of-kin is his adult son, who is the primary contact. He prefers morning appointments due to reliance on public transport.
On DRE, the prostate is smooth and non-nodular, consistent with a cT1c stage. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vitals and no signs of acute distress.
